note: Proof architecture: start at a vertex incident with an edge and greedily obtain a nonempty closed trail C. If C omits an edge, connectedness gives a vertex x of C incident with an omitted edge: if an omitted edge has no endpoint on C, follow a shortest path from one endpoint to V(C), whose last edge is omitted; if it has an endpoint on C, use that endpoint. The unused-edge spanning subgraph has even degrees because C consumes an even number of incidences at each vertex. A greedy unused-edge trail from x therefore closes to a nonempty D. Splice D into C at x, increasing the number of used edges. Repeat; finiteness forces an all-edge closed trail. For maximal rigor, phrase the greedy closure parity using incident edge-ends, and note loops count twice if the graph convention permits them.
